title: Speculative request grouping & prefix-reuse sentry: eval harness and rollback plan
creator: Alyssa Chen
description: Build a safeguard and evaluation pipeline (the 'sentry') for automated recommendations that enable speculative request grouping (a form of dynamic batching) and prefix/response reuse (KV-prefetch + prefix cache) aimed at reducing token cost. The sentry must produce conservative recommendations, run pre-apply shadowing against production traces, and enforce statistical acceptance thresholds on quality regressions before any automated apply. This ticket covers: design and implementation of the eval harness, definition of golden prompt anchors and behavioral checks, canary rollout strategy with abort/revert hooks, and the manual override/playbook for SRE/ML Engineers.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible eval harness that runs nightly and on-demand against historical production traces and synthetic edge cases
A curated set of golden anchors (100 prompts spanning formats: instruction, chat, code, summarization) with expected output fingerprints and fuzzy-matching tolerances
Statistical tests defined (e.g., paired bootstrap, A/B proportion tests) with clear thresholds for token-level and semantic regressions
Automated shadow run results surfaced in the Console with per-route delta metrics (latency, cost-per-request, semantic-fidelity) and pass/fail signal
Canary rollout configured with progressive traffic ramp, automatic abort on regression signal, and a one-click rollback action in the Console
Runbook and playbook documented with steps for manual inspection, escalation, and incident postmortem linkage
comments: 2026-03-05 - Alyssa Chen: Drafted ticket after architecture sync. Primary goal is to avoid noisy recommendations that save cost but erode quality. Focus first on a conservative acceptance surface and expand once stable.

2026-03-07 - Priya Kapur: Prototype eval harness runner implemented. It can reconstitute request sequences and run variants with and without prefix reuse. Observed ~12% token savings on a sampled e-comm trace but two high-severity semantic diffs on instruction prompts.
2026-03-09 - Marco Ruiz (review): Asked for clearer definition of the golden anchors tolerances and proposed adding a BLEURT-style embedding similarity check alongside token-delta thresholds.

2026-03-10 - Priya Kapur: Added dual-signal approach: (1) token/latency/cost regressions, (2) semantic delta via embedding cosine + per-prompt heuristics. Tuned initial thresholds to be conservative: require cost improvement >= 8% and semantic delta p-value < 0.01 to pass.

2026-03-12 - Design feedback from Zoe Park: Request grouping changes can affect streamed partial outputs. Need UX signal in Console to show 'streaming fidelity' metric and a sample stream diff viewer.

2026-03-13 - SRE note (Ethan Morales): Canary plan looks good; add alerting on increased error rates and KV cache hit ratio drops. Also require a fallback policy to the prior model variant if abort occurs.
